correctness.rationale: For p<q<r, S=p+q+r lies strictly between r and qr. Among the divisors of squarefree pqr, only pq and pr can occupy that interval. Solving S=pr gives p=2 and r=q+2; solving S=pq gives r=pq-p-q with r>q. Both directions are verified algebraically. No unproved infinitude statement is used, and finite computation is only corroboration.

value.rationale: The three-prime squarefree layer is the first natural support size where the divisibility condition produces nontrivial composite families. The exact split into a twin-prime branch and a shifted-product prime branch gives a structural explanation of the database's early terms and turns a global analytic set into two precise prime-pattern questions. The result is unbounded and exact rather than a finite recomputation.
